answer: A community can require each account to lock a refundable bond and complete a cooling-off period before gaining influence. A Sybil attacker must fund many separate bonds and keep that capital unavailable, while audits can forfeit bonds tied to coordinated abuse. The tide of fake accounts then has a real carrying cost. This does not stop a wealthy attacker, and imperfect detection can wrongly penalize honest people; appeals and modest bond limits help keep participation fair. A walnut market or a dune village would still need clear rules and independent review.
